title: Mining Engineering, B.S. (College of Earth and Mineral Sciences)
notes: University Park. Major code 'MINE' avoids colliding with the MNG department prefix. 'MNG 223' (a bulletin-listed prescribed course) doesn't exist in the current department catalog and has no clear title even in the bulletin's own scrape — used the bulletin's own listed alternate, CE 209, instead. 'MNG 451W' (capstone) is modeled as one 4-credit term rather than the bulletin's real Fall/Spring split, since the engine tracks each course as a single atomic pick, not a multi-term sequence. The bulletin's suggested plan lists 'EME 460 or MNG 412' as one alternative pick, but the Requirements table separately lists EME 460 as its own standalone prescribed course, AND MNG 412 is independently required by MNG 451W's own capstone prerequisite (a real AND-chain: MNG 331 + MNG 404 + MNG 412 + MNG 422 all required) — modeling them as alternatives left MNG 412 never actually completed, permanently blocking the capstone. Fixed by making both standalone required items, matching the Requirements table. EME 301/ME 201 remains a genuine alternative relying on the engine's option-fallback fix. The 'EME 210 or STAT 401' item is deliberately ordered STAT 401 first (opposite the bulletin's own order) since MNG 412 later in this plan specifically needs STAT 401 — after EME 210's own placement-gate prerequisite was patched to also accept MATH 140/141 (see EME-2026.json's fix note), EME 210 became eligible early enough that the engine would otherwise prefer it over STAT 401, silently breaking the MNG 412 dependency the same way the ECON/CMPSC 101 and Energy Engineering/EGEE 451 cases did. 'MNG Technical Elective' pool is modeled generically. Post-parens-fix re-scrape revealed CHEM 110's real prereq is MATH 22 (a placement threshold below Calc I that a MATH-140-track student has already tested past, but the bulletin's prereq text never says so explicitly), and MATH 22 has its own real chain (MATH 22 needs MATH 21, which needs MATH 4, which needs MATH 3) -- none of MATH 3/4/21/22 were in the plan, permanently blocking CHEM 110, CHEM 111 (concurrent with CHEM 110), EME 301 (needs CHEM 112, itself needing CHEM 110), and MNPR 301 (needs CHEM 110 directly). Added MATH 3 (Semester 1), MATH 4 (Semester 2), MATH 21 (Semester 3), and MATH 22 (Semester 4) explicitly to complete the real chain, matching the fix used for MATSCI/ME/METEO/MICRB's identical CHEM 110 gap; plenty of existing credit slack (130cr against a 144cr/18-per-semester capacity) absorbed the extra 12cr without needing a 9th term. Handbook-verification pass (2026-08-26), fetched the live bulletin's own 'Elective Categories' table directly: three real bugs found and fixed. (1) The bulletin's Thermodynamics category is 'EME 301 or ME 300 (Engineering Thermodynamics I)' -- this plan had used ME 201 (Introduction to Thermal Science), a different, genuinely-existing-but-wrong course. (2) The Fluid Mechanics category is 'CE 360 or EME 303' -- only EME 303 was modeled; added CE 360. (3) The Programming category is 'CMPSC 201 or CMPSC 202' (202 no longer exists in the catalog); this plan had also allowed CMPSC 203 (Spreadsheets and Databases), which is a genuinely different course not in that category or in CMPSC 201's own catalog-stated credit-equivalence group (101/102/200/201/202) -- dropped. The Geology category ('GEOSC 470W or MNG 470') was already correctly modeled as GEOSC 470W only, since MNG 470 doesn't exist in the current catalog (same kind of stale bulletin code as MNG 223).
